name: Maximum-Parent Profile Bounds under Free Coordinates
statement: For $D_t=C\times\{0,1\}^t$, $\mathcal F(C)+(t,t)\subseteq\mathcal F(D_t)\subseteq\bigcap_{u=0}^t(\mathcal F(C)+(u,t-u))$. Hence $h(D_t)=h(C)+t$, $h(D_t^c)=h(C^c)+t$, and $a(C)\le a(D_t)\le a(C)+t$. If $\mathcal F(C)$ has one minimal point, the first inclusion is equality and $a(D_t)=a(C)+t$.
proof: A two-control lift from a predecessor-parent-successor triple adds one free visible coordinate and one auxiliary while raising both parent ranks. Conversely, from any parent of $D_t$, fully reduce any $u$ free coordinates and project the other $t-u$; the resulting parent of $C$ has profile shifted by $(u,t-u)$. The exact least-rank and auxiliary bounds follow. A unique minimal original profile forces the translated quadrant.
comments: A parent can be symmetrized without changing parameters exactly when it arises from a nested chain of consecutive-rank maximum parents with one common marked section; numerical profile feasibility alone does not supply that chain.
